  "workflow_version": "GridResolveAIWorkflow v10",
  "case_state": "INTAKE",
  "dataset_version": "GRIDRESOLVE-SYNTH-2.0",
  "policy_version": "GRIDRESOLVE-POLICY-2.0",
  "intent": "Customer disputes a high bill and alleges meter malfunction causing an increased charge.",
  "investigation_type": "HIGH_BILL",
  "billing_period": {
    "primary_period_start": "2026-07-01",
    "primary_period_end": "2026-07-31"
  },
  "required_evidence": [
    "meter_reads for the disputed period and preceding period (register values and read types)",
    "billing history and bill calculation (rate components, billing days, applied charges) for at least 6 months",
    "meter diagnostics and event logs (tamper flags, self-test results)",
    "interval or detailed usage data if available (to analyze daily/weekly usage spikes)",
    "customer-provided information on occupancy/usage changes for the disputed period",
    "any prior adjustments or disputes"
  ],
  "missing_evidence": [
    "customer statement describing known usage changes or unusual events during July 2026",
    "interval (smart) meter data or daily usage breakdown for July 2026",
    "on-site meter inspection report or visual meter photos",
    "proof of recent meter maintenance or replacement (if any)",
    "billing determinant backup showing calculation details for the July 2026 bill"
  ],
  "account_evidence_required": true,
  "usage_analysis_required": true,
  "policy_lookup_required": true,
  "risk_flags": {
    "safety_risk": false,
    "legal_risk": false,
    "regulatory_risk": false,
    "fraud_risk": "LOW",
    "vulnerable_customer": false,
    "privacy_risk": false,
    "prompt_injection_risk": false,
    "real_data_contamination": false
  },
  "risk_class": "MEDIUM",
  "confidence": "HIGH",
  "human_review_candidate": false,
  "triage_summary": "Customer (SYN-ACCT-0003) reports a large increase in the July 2026 electric bill and alleges the meter is broken. Synthetic account records show billed kWh rose from 640 kWh (June) to 870 kWh (July) with matching actual register reads (41820 → 42690) and a passing remote self-test (2026-07-29) with no tamper flags. Investigation should focus on validating bill calculation (rates, billing days), analyzing interval/daily usage for an unexplained spike, obtaining customer usage/occupancy info and on-site inspection or photos if required, and reviewing meter diagnostics and event history. No prior adjustments or meter events are present in the provided records."
}

ROUTE_DECISION::GRIDRESOLVE_APPROVED

You told us your July 2026 electric bill was much higher and asked us to confirm whether the meter is broken and to fix the charge. We reviewed your account records and diagnostics and have not found evidence that the meter recorded incorrect energy. At this stage we have not applied any credits or other bill changes. A human reviewer will decide next steps if further inspection or an adjustment is needed.

What we reviewed
We reviewed the June and July 2026 billing records, the meter register reads taken on 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-31, the declared rate components used to calculate the bills, remote meter diagnostics from 2026-07-29, and the recent monthly usage history contained in your account records.

What we found
The meter register increased from 41,820 kWh on 2026-06-30 to 42,690 kWh on 2026-07-31, a change of 870 kWh. That register change matches the 870 kWh billed for July 2026. Using the stated energy rate and fixed charge reproduces the billed dollar amounts for June and July. A remote self-test on 2026-07-29 returned a PASS and the diagnostic record shows no tamper or register-fault flags. There are no recorded meter events in the supplied records.

Why your bill changed
Based on the records we reviewed, the higher July bill is explained by higher measured consumption for that month: billed kWh increased by 230 kWh compared with June and the meter register change equals the billed amount. We did not find evidence in the supplied diagnostics or event logs that the meter over-recorded usage. However, remote diagnostics have limits and do not absolutely rule out intermittent or installation issues.

What happens next
We will request additional information to narrow the cause. A human reviewer will be asked to (1) request interval (daily/hourly) usage data for July, (2) request a statement from you about any occupancy or appliance changes in July, and (3) offer a human-reviewed on-site meter inspection if you remain concerned. If new evidence shows a billing error or a confirmed meter fault, a Human Billing Supervisor must review and approve any credit or adjustment before it is applied.

What we need from you
Please tell us if anything changed at the property in July 2026 (guests, appliance purchases, HVAC use, or other events) and whether you can share any daily usage details or photos of the meter location. If you want an on-site inspection, tell us and we will arrange for a human-reviewed inspection to be scheduled. Do not disconnect or attempt to alter the meter; instead provide the requested information so we can investigate further.
